ChatGPT said:

That's because GitHub only renders images if the image path is correct and the image files are actually in your repository.

Let's check it.

Step 1: Is the image file in your repository?

Open your GitHub repository:
https://github.com/AzmeeraManjula/ecommerce-etl-pipeline

Do you see files like:

  • pipeline_architecture.png

  • dashboard.png

or an images folder containing them?

If No, that's why only the titles appear.

Step 2: Check your README

Your README should look something like this:

Markdown
## 📊 Pipeline Architecture

![Pipeline Architecture](pipeline_architecture.png)

## 📁 Project Structure

```text
ecommerce-etl-pipeline/
├── data/
├── docs/
├── scripts/
├── sql/
├── README.md
└── .gitignore

If the image name doesn't exactly match the file in GitHub (including uppercase/lowercase), GitHub won't display it.

---

### Step 3: Verify the image location

If your image is inside an `images` folder, the README should be:

```markdown
![Pipeline Architecture](images/pipeline_architecture.png)

not

Markdown
![Pipeline Architecture](pipeline_architecture.png)

I can find the problem quickly

Please either:

  1. Paste your README.md here or

  2. Share the GitHub link to the README page (which you've already done) and tell me whether the images are in the root folder or inside an images folder.

I'll tell you the exact line to fix. It usually takes less than a minute.

ChatGPT said:

That's exactly why GitHub is only showing the headings and not the content.

There are two different things:

1. Pipeline Architecture (Image)

This is not created automatically. It's a diagram that you need to create (for example, in Draw.io or Canva) and save as an image.

A simple architecture diagram for your project could look like this:

Kaggle Olist Dataset (9 CSV Files)
                │
                ▼
      Python Data Cleaning
                │
                ▼
      SQL Transformations
                │
                ▼
        SQLite Database
                │
                ▼
     PySpark Aggregations
                │
                ▼
     Tableau Dashboard

Save it as pipeline_architecture.png and upload it to your GitHub repository.

Then your README will display it using:

Markdown
## 📊 Pipeline Architecture

![Pipeline Architecture](pipeline_architecture.png)

2. Project Folder Structure

This doesn't need an image. It's usually written as text in the README.

For your project, you can use something like:

ecommerce-etl-pipeline/
│
├── data/
│   ├── raw/
│   ├── processed/
│   └── ecommerce.db
│
├── docs/
│
├── scripts/
│   ├── explore_data.py
│   ├── 02_transform.py
│   ├── 03_pyspark_transform.py
│   ├── 04_load.py
│   └── 05_automate.py
│
├── sql/
│
├── README.md
├── .gitignore
└── ecommerce_dashboard.twb

GitHub will render this as a code block—no image is needed.

My recommendation

Since you're polishing this project for your portfolio, I recommend:

  • ✅ Add a pipeline architecture diagram (it's worth it because recruiters like visual workflows).

  • ✅ Keep the folder structure as text in the README (this is the standard approach).

If you'd like, I can also create a professional pipeline architecture diagram for your ETL project that matches your GitHub theme. You can upload it directly to your repository and use it in your README.
